title: CardinalPay POC - Infosec Q&A and Evidence Log
body:
Purpose: quick-working Q&A and evidence tracker for the CardinalPay POC (Dedicated + Private deployment options). This doc is intended to collect answers to the infosec questionnaire sent by CardinalPay, list concrete evidence artifacts we can share, and call out unresolved gaps and owners. Treat as living — aim to hand off to engagements/sales as the single source for evidence files for the customer audit window.

Summary / context:
- POC scope: dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 with optional VPC peering to CardinalPay staging environment. Short lived (8 weeks) POC to validate latencies, throughput, and data isolation.
- CardinalPay security asks: encryption at rest/in-transit proof, access control reviews, logging/retention, architecture diagrams, pen-test results or vulnerability scans, SOC2 mapping where available, and sample audit artifacts for a limited time window.
- Our compliance posture: Redwood has SOC2 Type II in prod; Dedicated/Private deployments leverage customer's network controls and Redwood private control plane for management traffic.

Contents of this doc:
1) Completed Q&A (customer questionnaire items we have final answers for)
2) Evidence items (what we will attach/evidence id -> file to produce)
3) Gaps / open questions (items that need follow-up)
4) Action items + owners + ETA
5) Fast references to internal tickets / confluence pages

1) Completed Q&A (short answers suitable for inclusion in the customer questionnaire)
Q: Where are customer data and model artifacts stored for the POC?
A: Model artifacts and customer prompts/inputs are stored on Dedicated instances in the customer-dedicated S3 prefix (us-west-2). Management plane metadata is stored in the customer-specific namespace in our private control plane; sensitive keys are never stored in plaintext and access to the control plane is restricted by RBAC and IP allowlists for the POC.

Q: How is data encrypted at rest?
A: At rest data is encrypted using AES-256. S3 buckets used for the POC are configured with default encryption using a dedicated KMS CMK (Key Alias: alias/redwood/cardinalpay-poc). KMS grant logs and key rotation policy are available on request.

Q: How is network traffic secured?
A: All network traffic between Redwood runtime nodes and CardinalPay VPC uses TLS 1.3. For Private deployments with VPC peering, we use mutual TLS for control plane traffic and enforce SG rules to restrict ingress. Transit encryption for inter-node traffic is enforced via mTLS and internal cert rotation every 30 days.

Q: Who has access to the POC environment and how is access audited?
A: Access is granted via SSO (Okta) with SCIM provisioning scoped to the POC group. Admin access is limited to named engineers. All user logins and API token usage events are captured in the audit log and forwarded to CardinalPay's Logstash endpoint during the test window.

Q: Do you run vulnerability scans / pentests on POC infra?
A: We run weekly vulnerability scans (Qualys) on nodes that host the POC. SRE runs container image scans during build time (Trivy). Full external pentests are offered as an add-on and can be scheduled; for this POC CardinalPay has requested to rely on our internal scan reports.

2) Evidence items (files to attach to the questionnaire / to hand to CardinalPay security)
- Evidence 01: Architecture diagram (file: card-pay-arch-v1.png) — shows VPC peering, private control plane, and data flow (owner: Lucas Meyer).
- Evidence 02: KMS key policy + key rotation log (file: cardinalpay-kms-policy-2026-02-12.pdf) — export of key policy, IAM principals with grants (owner: Priya Natarajan).
- Evidence 03: S3 bucket policy and bucket encryption config + sample object metadata (file: s3-bucket-config-cardinalpay.json) — includes bucket lifecycle / retention info (owner: Miguel Alvarez).
- Evidence 04: Access audit extract (CSV, 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-14) — Okta authentication events and API key usage (file: access-audit-cardinalpay-20260214.csv) (owner: Ava Chen).
- Evidence 05: Vulnerability scan summary (Qualys export) — node-level findings and remediation status (file: qly-scan-summary-cardinalpay-week3.pdf) (owner: Emma Singh).
- Evidence 06: Network ACL / Security Group snapshots and NACL ruleset export (file: secgroup-nacls-cardinalpay.txt) (owner: Lucas Meyer).
- Evidence 07: Runtime config snapshot (inference-engine config, batching, KV cache settings) and model inventory list (file: runtime-config-cardinalpay-2026-02-14.yaml) (owner: Miguel Alvarez).
- Evidence 08: SLA excerpt and POC statement of work (file: poc-sow-cardinalpay-v2.pdf) — includes availability objective for Dedicated nodes during the POC (owner: Sales Ops).

Stored location plan: evidence artifacts will be uploaded to a signed S3 bundle and we will share a time-limited download link. For extremely sensitive artifacts (e.g., KMS grants list), we will share via the CardinalPay secure upload portal.

3) Gaps / open questions (rapid list)
- G1: CardinalPay asked for a copy of the latest SOC2 Type II report. We can provide a redacted copy (legal clearance required). Owner: Legal (TBD). ETA: 2026-02-21.
- G2: They requested historical log retention beyond 90 days for the POC window (180 days). Need SRE to confirm storage and cost implications. Owner: Emma Singh. ETA: 2026-02-20.
- G3: Request for a network packet capture from a single request showing TLS negotiation. We need to confirm privacy/compliance for sharing PCAPs. Owner: Lucas Meyer + Legal. ETA: 2026-02-22.
- G4: They asked for proof of HSM usage for KMS keys. Our KMS is cloud-managed (AWS KMS) with HSM-backed keys; need to produce vendor documentation and key lineage. Owner: Priya Natarajan. ETA: 2026-02-23.

4) Action items, owners, and current status
- A1: Produce architecture diagram updated to show VPC CIDR ranges used for the POC. Owner: Lucas Meyer. Status: in_progress. ETA: 2026-02-16.
- A2: Export of Okta SCIM group membership and recent auth logs (14 day window). Owner: Ava Chen. Status: done. File: access-audit-cardinalpay-20260214.csv
- A3: Pull S3 bucket lifecycle and encryption config; include a sample object metadata row to demonstrate SSE-KMS. Owner: Miguel Alvarez. Status: done. File: s3-bucket-config-cardinalpay.json
- A4: Collate vulnerability scan PDF and triage status (remediated / in progress). Owner: Emma Singh. Status: in_progress. ETA: 2026-02-18.
- A5: Legal to prepare redacted SOC2 artifact approval and sharing note. Owner: Legal (contact: Jordan Reyes). Status: blocked (legal review). ETA: 2026-02-21.

5) Recommended language for the customer questionnaire fields (copy/paste friendly)
- Encryption at rest: "All customer data stored as part of the POC is encrypted at rest using AES-256 via AWS KMS. A dedicated CMK (alias/redwood/cardinalpay-poc) is used for the POC; key usage and grants can be reviewed upon request under an NDA."
- Encryption in transit: "All network traffic is encrypted using TLS 1.3. Inter-node and control plane traffic uses mutual TLS and certificates rotated on a 30-day cadence."
- Access controls: "Access to the POC environment uses SSO (Okta) with scoped SCIM groups. Admin access is restricted and audited; we provide audit logs for the POC time window."

6) Notes to self / meeting prep for the 2026-02-19 workshop with CardinalPay security
- Bring the updated architecture diagram and KMS policy export.
- Have a short demo-ready sequence showing: (1) create a test request against Dedicated endpoint, (2) show audit log entry appearing in the Logstash forwarder, (3) demonstrate S3 object metadata showing SSE-KMS.
- Expect questions on data residency and model caching: be ready to show that KV cache does not persist outside dedicated nodes and cache eviction is deterministic per policy.

7) Quick references and internal links
- Confluence: CardinalPay POC master spec (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/CardinalPay+POC+Spec)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/214 (VPC peering and security group changes)
- Tickets: POCP-112 (sales request), SEC-4231 (security questionnaire)

8) Final checklist before sharing the package to CardinalPay security (owner sign-off required)
- [ ] KMS policy export (Priya)
- [ ] Architecture diagram with annotated CIDRs (Lucas)
- [ ] Okta auth export and explanation (Ava)
- [ ] Vulnerability scan summary with remediation notes (Emma)
- [ ] Redacted SOC2 availability or letter from Legal (Jordan)
- [ ] SOW and SLA excerpt (Sales Ops)

Appendix: sample artifact names and short descriptions (what we will include in the S3 bundle)
- cardinalpay_architecture_v1.png — network diagram, private control plane, peering arrows.
- cardinalpay_kms_policy_20260212.pdf — KMS policy, key alias, and key usage grants.
- cardinalpay_s3_config_20260214.json — S3 bucket policy + encryption metadata.
- cardinalpay_access_audit_20260214.csv — Okta auth and API key events (redacted PII).
- cardinalpay_vulnscan_week3.pdf — Qualys summary, CVEs, remediation notes.

Open decisions / escalation path:
- If Legal does not approve SOC2 redaction before the workshop, bring a statement from Legal with expected timing and offer a live readout instead. (Escalate to Head of Security if blocked >48 hrs).
- For any request to view raw PCAPs or full unredacted auth logs, require an executed DPA + NDA and explicit SOW line item.

History / changelog:
